title: HavenBank security onboarding protocols and artifacts
content:
Purpose:
This note captures our recommended security onboarding protocol, an evidence checklist, and the raw workshop notes from the initial HavenBank POC kickoff (Nov 2025). Designed to be a practical playbook for the SE team + security SMEs to accelerate evidence collection and reduce back-and-forth during audit prep.

Background/context:
- Customer: HavenBank (mid-size regional bank) evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for internal LLM assistants and document processing.
- POC goals: demonstrate deployment in customer VPC with KMS integration, RBAC, and audit logging; satisfy initial vendor security questionnaire for SOC2-lite procurement review.
- Constraint: customer security team requires artifact delivery within 4 weeks of kickoff (tight).

Scope of this doc:
1) Minimum evidence set to satisfy initial vendor security questionnaire (vendor-lite).
2) Mapping from questionnaire controls to Redwood artifacts, and where to pull/log exports.
3) Workshop notes (raw) from 2025-11-20 kickoff and follow-ups.
4) Next actions and owners (quick actionable list).

Quick evidence checklist (minimum deliverables for first pass):
- Architecture diagram (network flows, subnets, peering) — file: havenbank-arch-v1.png (s3).
- KMS integration proof: KMS policy snapshot + example envelope decryption logs (redacted).
- RBAC matrix: list of Redwood roles mapped to IAM groups (CSV).
- Audit log sample: 7-day slice of control-plane API calls + time-synced application logs (gz).
- SIEM export instructions: sample syslog config and test event.
- Pen test summary: latest infra vuln-scan report (summary page).
- Hardening checklist: OS image baseline + AIDE/Integrity check configs.
- Data flow TOC: where tokens/PII may touch, and TTL/retention settings.

Control -> Evidence mapping (where to find artifacts):
- Network segmentation (control): VPC peering diagram & subnet table (s3/havenbank/arch).
- Key management (control): KMS policy + CMK ARN + alias listing (cloud-kms export).
- Access control (control): IAM role mapping csv + last 90-day console access audit (cloudtrail extract).
- Logging & monitoring (control): Cloudwatch/Datadog link, sample alert rule, 7-day log archive (s3).
- Change management (control): PR/approval links (github PR 412) and deployment runbook (confluence).
- Vulnerability management (control): Image scan report (anchore/clair export).

Notes on redaction and customer confidentiality:
- Remove customer PII before handing artifacts. Use placeholder IDs (HAVEN-XXXX) and include a redaction manifest file.
- Logs: truncate request/response bodies, preserve headers/timestamps. Provide an authenticated viewer link rather than raw dumps where feasible.

Workshop notes (raw, 2025-11-20 kickoff + 2025-11-27 deep-dive):
- Attendees: HavenBank SecOps (J. Morales, R. Chen), Platform (K. Singh), Redwood: Aisha Patel (SE lead), Marcus Lee (security engineering), Sofia Gutierrez (solutions).
- J. Morales: primary checklist is KMS + network isolation. Wants proof of HSM-backed key storage for production; for POC, CMK with rotation policy acceptable.
- R. Chen: SIEM ingestion — needs JSON syslog prototype by week 2. Will provide Splunk index name and sample ingest key.
- K. Singh: asked about in-transit protections between customer app and Redwood runtime — we confirmed mTLS and customer-managed certs supported in private deployment. Action: send TLS config template.
- Marcus: identified three demo artifacts missing from our bucket: (1) AIDE checksums, (2) sample cloudtrail query for auth failures, (3) retention config for model cache.
- Sofia: flagged potential delay — customer wants signed evidence (attestation) for RBAC. We proposed an internal signed statement + artifact references; customer requested legal review.

Decisions made during workshop:
- For POC we will use CMKs (Cloud KMS) with rotation every 90 days; production recommendation will be HSM-backed.
- Provide a 7-day log export (redacted) and a separate policy doc describing full retention/archival schedule.
- SE will package artifacts into an S3 staging area with IAM-limited access for HavenBank SecOps.

Open questions / risks:
- Attestation/Signing: legal needs to approve our attestation language. Risk: legal review could add 2+ weeks.
- Pen-test scope: customer may require third-party pen test for production; budget/timing TBD.
- HSM availability in customer region (AP-SOUTHEAST) — ops to confirm.

Action items (owner -> deliverable -> due):
- Marcus Lee -> produce AIDE checksum bundle + integrity verification readme -> 2025-11-24 -> JIRA:SEC-742.
- Aisha Patel -> TLS config template + mTLS example for private deploy -> 2025-11-25 -> attach to confluence page.
- Sofia Gutierrez -> assemble redaction manifest + create S3 staging layout -> 2025-11-26 -> s3 path provided to customer.
- Ethan Zhang -> export 7-day redacted audit logs (cloudtrail + app logs) -> 2025-11-28 -> to s3.
- Product/Security -> draft attestation language for RBAC -> 2025-12-03 -> legal review required.

Packaging & delivery plan:
- Week 1: collect artifacts + internal review (SE + security).
- Week 2: apply redaction, generate manifest, upload to customer-limited s3 staging.
- Week 3: customer review + remediate any follow-ups.
- Delivery artifact set: zip of artifacts, redaction-manifest.txt, signed cover email (templated).

Appendix: sample anonymized log snippet (redacted)
[2025-11-15T14:02:03Z] AUTH_SUCCESS user=HAVEN-123 action=assumeRole role=redwood-se-poctest src_ip=10.2.3.45
[2025-11-15T14:12:22Z] API_CALL user=redwood-service action=CreateInferenceRequest model=gptx-serve seq=128 latency_ms=22
[REDACTED] payload truncated

Slack refs / internal threads:
- #poc-havenbank thread (link: slack workspace) — see pinned messages for drafts.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (contains subnet/route updates used in the diagram).

Packaging checklist for handoff (SE):
- Ensure each artifact has a one-line description and source (who created it).
- Create a small README.md in the staging s3 with redaction rules and contact person.
- Add a short-recorded walkthrough (5–8m) explaining the artifacts (MP4).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the POC artifact bundle minimal; customers get nervous with large dumps. Prioritize control evidence over raw telemetry.
- If legal delays on attestation, provide interim statement with clear expiry and add escalation path.

If any reviewer wants to re-order or add items, leave comments inline or tag Marcus.

-- Aisha P. (SE lead)
